archetypes.name: Evaluate a Direct Variation Rule
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.8 — Modeling Using Variation
archetypes.coreConcept: In direct variation, the dependent quantity is a constant multiple of a power of the input.
archetypes.mentalModel: Keep the variation constant and exponent fixed, then substitute the requested input.

cognitiveTraps.description: Using the exponent as a multiplier instead of raising the input to that power.

archetypes.figureNone: The rule and input are given explicitly; the exercise is substitution into a symbolic variation model, not graph interpretation.

archetypes.name: Evaluate an Inverse Variation Rule
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.8 — Modeling Using Variation
archetypes.coreConcept: Inverse variation divides the constant by the specified power of the input.
archetypes.mentalModel: Increasing the input changes the denominator; preserve the reciprocal structure when substituting.

cognitiveTraps.description: Multiplying by the input power instead of dividing by it.

archetypes.figureNone: The inverse rule is explicit and the task is a direct substitution check; a graph would not add information.

archetypes.name: Calibrate a Direct Variation Constant
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.8 — Modeling Using Variation
archetypes.coreConcept: A known input-output pair determines the constant of variation; the calibrated rule can then predict a new output.
archetypes.mentalModel: Divide the known output by the known input power to identify k, then apply the same rule to the new input.

cognitiveTraps.description: Scaling the output by the input ratio instead of the ratio raised to the variation power.

archetypes.figureNone: The unknown constant is inferred from a data pair, so a graph could expose the model being tested instead of the calibration steps.

archetypes.name: Solve a Joint Variation Model
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.8 — Modeling Using Variation
archetypes.coreConcept: Joint variation combines direct powers of some variables with inverse powers of others under one shared constant.
archetypes.mentalModel: Write one constant times every direct factor divided by every inverse factor; calibrate the constant once and keep the exponents attached to their variables.

cognitiveTraps.description: Multiplying by a variable that the model states varies inversely.

archetypes.figureNone: The item is an algebraic multi-variable substitution; plotting one variable would require arbitrary fixed values for the others and would not aid the requested calculation.
